title: Corpus report
description: The output of Corpus.Collect: every shard of the job's task list in task order with how it ended - the verdict of its accepted result with its product blobs and content hash, Disputed (its copies disagreed and no majority of three machines settled it) or NoResult with a fixed reason (no machine returned a result that could be accepted) - and the aggregate over the accepted results. The shards, their indexes and their URLs are the server's own task list; nothing a node returns can add, remove or rename one. Version 3: version 2 took the index and the URL from the node's result and chose between the executions of a sampled shard by their content hashes.

controller.description: The controller version that wrote the report.

tasks.description: The shards of the job: the task list Corpus.Split made, whatever came back.

verdicts.description: Shards per verdict, Disputed and NoResult among them.

single_execution.description: Shards whose accepted result is one machine's word: not sampled, or the copy came back as a node fault. Nothing compared it.

rejected_results.description: Values the server dropped on arrival: under no ticket of this job and round, naming another shard, claiming another controller version, shaped as no honest node shapes a result, or at odds with the task. The integrity document counts them by reason.

repairs.description: Shards sent out once more because the first round left them without a result (a node fault, a dropped value).

disputes.description: Shards whose copies disagreed: each was run again on up to three machines.

disputes_resolved.description: Of those, the ones settled: one result was returned by the most machines, two at least, without a tie. The others are Disputed.

drops.description: Documents dropped per rule, summed over the completed shards.

languages.description: Documents out per ISO 639-3 code, summed over the completed shards.

unsupported_languages.description: Documents dropped as language_unsupported, by where they were nearest: the code of a language the pack knows and does not support, past_limit:<code> for a supported language the document lies past the limit of (a language the pack has no profile for, or text too unlike its own), no_profile for text that shares no n-gram with any profile. Sums to the drop language_unsupported; absent from reports of controllers before 0.2.0. Summed over the completed shards.

pdf_in.description: PDF responses the PDF stage took (WARC; present only where a shard met a PDF, like every pdf_* count).

pdf_truncated.description: Of those, the ones the crawler cut short (WARC-Truncated); read all the same.

pdf_extracted.description: PDFs that gave at least one page-range document.

pdf_documents.description: The page-range documents made (url#page=a-b); each also counts in documents_extracted.

pdf_pages_cut.description: Pages longer than a document may be (5,000 words), cut after the last line that fits.

pdf_running_lines.description: Lines removed as running headers and footers.

pdf_fuel.description: Fuel the PDF sandbox burned, counted from each run's _start: the same on every node.

funnel.description: The run's funnel over the completed shards: the records read, the documents extracted, the documents left after the language stage, the line stage and the quality filter, and the documents out (equal to quality); dropped sums the drops by the stage that applies them (extract counts records and PDFs that gave no document, beside the funnel; the others count documents). Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0.

output.description: What the run kept on the server: full, or stats_and_hashes (no text, no signatures: text_blob and signatures_blob are "", and Corpus.Dedup refuses the run). Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0 (they kept everything).

minhash.description: The MinHash parameters every shard's signatures were made with (kept or not); absent when no shard made signatures or the shards differ (each shard then says its own), and from reports of controllers before 0.3.0 (the defaults).

url.description: The shard's URL, from the server's task.

verdict.description: How the shard ended. The first seven are verdicts on the shard, the same on any honest node. Disputed: its copies disagreed and three machines did not settle it; it has no product and is out of the counts. NoResult: no machine returned a result that could be accepted, after one more try; reason says why. A node's own trouble is never a verdict.

reason.description: Present on NoResult: node_fault (every machine that held the shard returned it as a fault of its own; faults names the codes), rejected (everything returned for it was dropped), missing (nothing came back under its tickets).

executions.description: How many results the accepted one rests on: 1 is one machine's word, 2 a pair that agreed, 2 or 3 the majority of a dispute; 0 for Disputed and NoResult.

faults.description: Present when a node returned the shard as a fault of its own in any round: the fault codes, each once. A shard with a fault and a result was made by another machine or on the second try.

text_blob.description: Blob id of the zstd JSON lines, or "".

signatures_blob.description: Blob id of the signatures, or "".

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the uncompressed JSON lines: the identity a re-execution must reproduce.

error.description: A fixed code, never free text: why the shard did not complete (http_ and the three digits of the origin's status, hash_mismatch, body_truncated, oversized, oversized_unpacked, not_warc, bad_compression, origin_not_allowed, origin_not_listed, origin_address, origin_redirect, no_language_model, language_model_refused, task_invalid), truncated on a completed shard whose file ends inside a record, or empty.

runtime_target.description: The operating system and architecture the shard ran on, e.g. "linux-x64" ("" from a controller before it was reported). A platform, never a machine.

degree.description: Shards the node processed at once (its cores, bounded by memory): the context of process_ms (0 when not reported).

minhash.description: The MinHash parameters the shard's signatures were made with; present when signatures were made, kept or not (absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0, whose signatures carry the defaults).

signatures_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the shard's signatures blob as the node made it, kept or not (under stats_and_hashes it is made and hashed, not uploaded); empty when no signature was made. Absent from reports of controllers before 0.3.0.

bytes_produced.description: Bytes of the compressed text product; under output stats_and_hashes the size the product had on the node before it was deleted.

wait_ms.description: Time the shard waited on the node for a download slot and a processing slot.

drops.description: Documents dropped per rule; the PDF stage's are pdf_encrypted, pdf_unreadable, pdf_no_pages, pdf_fuel, pdf_memory, pdf_trap, pdf_error, pdf_oversized and pdf_empty.

unsupported_languages.description: Documents dropped as language_unsupported, by where they were nearest: the code of a language the pack knows and does not support, past_limit:<code> for a supported language the document lies past the limit of (a language the pack has no profile for, or text too unlike its own), no_profile for text that shares no n-gram with any profile. Sums to the drop language_unsupported; absent from reports of controllers before 0.2.0.

pdf_in.description: PDF responses the PDF stage took (WARC; present only where a shard met a PDF, like every pdf_* count).

pdf_truncated.description: Of those, the ones the crawler cut short (WARC-Truncated); read all the same.

pdf_extracted.description: PDFs that gave at least one page-range document.

pdf_documents.description: The page-range documents made (url#page=a-b); each also counts in documents_extracted.

pdf_pages_cut.description: Pages longer than a document may be (5,000 words), cut after the last line that fits.

pdf_running_lines.description: Lines removed as running headers and footers.

pdf_fuel.description: Fuel the PDF sandbox burned, counted from each run's _start: the same on every node.

counts.description: Name to count, names in ordinal order.
